_meta.indication: GnRH receptor antagonist indicated for treatment of patients with advanced prostate cancer.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, active-controlled study with three treatment arms (degarelix 240/160 mg, degarelix 240/80 mg, and leuprolide 7.5 mg) for 12 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with prostate cancer; 20% had metastatic disease and 80% had non-metastatic disease (locally advanced, localized, or PSA relapse only after primary definitive therapy).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Probability of testosterone ≤ 0.5 ng/mL from Day 28 to Day 364 in each arm.
pivotal_trials.n: 610 patients in the active-controlled analysis (degarelix 240/160 mg N=202, degarelix 240/80 mg N=207, leuprolide 7.5 mg N=201).
pivotal_trials.result: Probability of medical castration (testosterone ≤ 0.5 ng/mL, Day 28–364) was 98.3% (95% CI 94.8–99.4%) for degarelix 240/160 mg, 97.2% (93.5–98.8%) for degarelix 240/80 mg, and 96.4% (92.5–98.2%) for leuprolide 7.5 mg.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were injection site reactions, hot flashes, increased weight, and transaminase/GGT increases. Injection site adverse events occurred in 35% (240/80 mg arm) vs <1% leuprolide; hot flash 26% vs 21% leuprolide. Injection site pain 28%, erythema 17%, swelling 6%.
target_moa: Degarelix is a GnRH receptor antagonist that binds reversibly to pituitary GnRH receptors, reducing release of gonadotropins and consequently testosterone.

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee because the key study used an established surrogate endpoint and did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues.

basis.text: The application received a Standard Review priority designation.

summary.text: Degarelix was granted regular (standard-review) approval based on Phase 3 Study CS21 using the established surrogate endpoint of biochemical testosterone castration; the application was not referred to an advisory committee, with one required postmarketing study (extension study CS21A) for long-term safety.

Study CS21 was an open-label, randomized, active-controlled, three-arm, international, phase 3 trial of monthly degarelix vs leuprolide (Lupron Depot) in patients with prostate cancer in whom androgen deprivation therapy was warranted.

This application was not referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee for review because the key study used an established surrogate endpoint, and the results of the study did not raise significant issues with respect to the efficacy and safety of degarelix in the intended population.

requirement.text: Complete the ongoing extension study FE200486 CS21A, an open-label, multicenter extension study evaluating the long-term safety and tolerability of degarelix one month dosing regimen in prostate cancer patients requiring androgen ablation therapy.

citations.quote: To complete the ongoing extension study FE200486 CS21A entitled “An Open-Label, Multi-Center, Extension Study, Evaluating the Long-Term Safety and Tolerability of Degarelix One Month Dosing Regimen in Patients with Prostate Cancer Requiring Androgen Ablation Therapy”.
